correctedState:
`strictAllowlist` has no reader (0 hits repo-wide with `grep -a`), and that is correct as a fact — but it is not a standalone divergence. It is one unchecked task in R19, the egress-proxy unit PARKED by dated owner decision 2026-07-28 ("нужно всё разрешить, ограничения будут потом"), recorded at `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-25-nessy-claude-parity-audit.md:690` with the plan retained at `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-28-egress-proxy.md:26`.

The setting is unimplementable in isolation: Claude's per-host allowlist is proxy-enforced outside the sandbox (`sandboxing.md:321`), and this fork ships no egress proxy, so `SandboxEgressDecisionV1` is `'open' | 'denied'` only (`sandbox-settings.ts:830`), a measured platform limit (`:845-873`). With no per-host prompt for sandboxed commands, "deny instead of prompt" has nothing to convert. The gap is disclosed rather than silent: `resolveSandboxNetworkEnforcement` (`:900`) reports each configured domain rule as `unenforceable`, and `/doctor` prints `sandboxed-command egress: open`.

Correction to the row's own text: `allowManagedDomainsOnly` is NOT managed-only in this fork — `sandbox-settings.ts:599` ORs it across every settings layer by design (`:85-87`), so any layer can arm the fail-closed lever.

Actionable residual, if any: unparking R19 (build the proxy), at which point `strictAllowlist` becomes implementable along with first-use approval, wildcard matching and the project-layer-ignored rule the plan already specifies. No isolated fix exists.
